title: feat(scenarios): --effort reaches claude --effort, and every turn records the effort it asked for
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao9j8wzUEy12QQraci54TCrP)_

epic:#33595#1 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzVKmz2fkqywcpUp6f

Clause-②: yes (widening) — new CLI flags `--effort`, `--author-effort`, `--ask-effort` (the `objectstack-scenarios run` bin and `run-scenarios`, both through `runner/cli.ts` `main`); new exports `CLAUDE_EFFORT_ENV` and `effortLevelsFromHelp` (`./runner`, via `src/runner/index.ts` re-exporting `driver.ts`); new optional fields `ClaudeCodeDriverOptions.effort` / `authorEffort` / `askEffort`, `DriverInfo.authorEffort` / `askEffort` (`driver.ts`), `ExternalDriverOptions.effort` / `authorEffort` / `askEffort` and `ExternalLimits.effort` (`drivers/external.ts`), `TurnProcess.requestedEffort` (`transcript.ts`), `TurnSummary.requestedEffort` (`orchestrate.ts`), `HalfScores.build.author.requestedEffort` and the field `ModelTally.requestedEfforts` (`scorecard.ts`), all reached through `./runner`
Metadata-protocol: none

Fixes #33739

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:跑分器新增 `--effort`(以及分开设定的 `--author-effort` / `--ask-effort`),把档位原样传给 `claude --effort`;每一轮都记下自己要的档位,评分表在「所用模型」旁边标出 `effort xx`。
- 为什么改:你问过「现在用的 effort 分别是什么,需要对照测试吗」——此前跑分器不传档位,所有轮次都跑在 CLI 默认档,记录也说不出是哪一档,模型对比分不开模型与档位;M2 收尾的 effort 对照要靠这张卡。
- 风险与回滚:实测 CLI 遇到拼错的档位只警告、照默认档跑且退出 0,所以跑分器开跑前按 CLI 自己 `--help` 列出的档位校验,不在表里就拒绝;环境变量 `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` 在 CLI 里压过 `--effort`,所以不再传给子进程,没给档位旗时改由它作为 `--effort` 传入并记录(效果不变、记录变真)。codex 没有对应旗,三个旗都拒绝;回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/driver.ts` 的 `ClaudeCodeDriver` 构造函数与 `turnEnv()`(档位校验、去掉环境变量);`src/runner/cli.ts` 的 `makeDriver`(codex/recorded 拒绝);`src/runner/scorecard.ts` 的 `modelCell` / `authorCell`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 -t effort test/runner`,预期 9 个用例全过(其余跳过)。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **Flags** (`runner/cli.ts`): `--effort LEVEL` sets every live turn, `--author-effort` / `--ask-effort` set the authoring turns and the question/operation turns apart, each in place of `--effort` — the same shape as `--model` / `--author-model` / `--ask-model`. A value that is empty or starts with `-` is refused at parse time.
- **Claude driver** (`runner/driver.ts`, `ClaudeCodeDriver` only): the turn's argv gains `--effort LEVEL`, and `meta.process.requestedEffort` records it. Measured on this box (`claude --version` = 2.1.325):
  - `claude --help` lists `--effort LEVEL` with `(low, medium, high, xhigh, max)`.
  - An unknown level is not an error: `claude -p --effort bogus` printed `Warning: Unknown --effort value 'bogus' — ignoring it and using the default effort. Valid values: low, medium, high, xhigh, max.` on stderr and exited 0. So the driver reads the levels off the CLI's own `--help` (`effortLevelsFromHelp`) when an effort is asked for and refuses one it does not list before any card runs; a CLI whose help has no `--effort` refuses every effort flag. Nothing is read when no effort is asked for.
  - The stream reports no served effort (the init line carries only `per_turn_effort_active: true`), so the record holds the asked-for level only.
  - The CLI's own code (2.1.325) resolves `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` ahead of the value it is passed, so with the variable set, `--effort low` would run at the variable's level while the record said `low`. The driver therefore removes the variable from every turn's environment, and with no effort flag reads its level (`auto` / `unset` / empty ⇒ default) and passes it as `--effort`, validated the same way.
- **External driver** (`runner/drivers/external.ts`): `limits.effort` carries the level as typed; the record states it. The contract stays `objectstack-scenario-driver/1` (an optional key, sent only when a flag is given).
- **Codex** (`makeDriver`): refused, measured on `codex-cli 0.167.0` (installed into a scratch dir for the reading): `codex exec --help` has no effort flag; the config key `model_reasoning_effort` exists, but `-c model_reasoning_effort="bogus"` started a turn exactly as `low` / `xhigh` / `max` did, so no level name could be checked offline. `--effort`, `--author-effort`, `--ask-effort` are refused with "has no equivalent in the Codex CLI: `codex exec` takes no effort flag", as the turn caps are.
- **Replay**: `recorded:` refuses the three flags through `LIVE_FLAGS`, as it refuses the model flags. `RecordedDriver` is untouched.
- **Record and scorecard**: `TurnSummary.requestedEffort` per turn; the record's `env.driver` carries `authorEffort` / `askEffort`; `ModelTally.requestedEfforts`. The author rows read `… · claude-haiku-5-5 · effort xhigh` and the `Run · model` rows `claude-haiku-5-5 ×24 · effort medium`; a turn that asked for none shows none.
- **Docs**: the runner README gains an **Effort** paragraph, two command examples, the codex flag line and the external `limits` line; `cli.ts`'s header (the CLI help) lists the three flags.

## Tests

- `test/runner/units.test.ts` (stand-in `claude`, which now answers `--help` with the 2.1.325 `--effort` entry and an `ENV` turn): the argv on every turn, the two kinds apart, one kind alone, no flag ⇒ no `--effort`; the variable never reaches a turn (flag wins, env alone becomes the flag, `auto` / `UNSET` ⇒ none); a level the help does not list (`turbo`, `High`, a misspelt variable) and a help with no `--effort` are refused, every listed level accepted; empty values and replay refused; `effortLevelsFromHelp` on the measured help text.
- `test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts`: `runCard` with a driver stamping efforts — per-turn `requestedEffort`, `ModelTally.requestedEfforts`, the author and Run · model cells, `env.driver`; a half with no model reported still shows its effort.
- `test/runner/external-driver.test.ts`: `limits.effort` per kind and absent with no flag. `test/runner/codex-driver.test.ts`: the three flags refused.

## Acceptance notes

- `transcript.ts` is outside the claim's listed file surface (inside the epic's territory): `TurnProcess.requestedEffort` sits beside `requestedModel` there, the field the live drivers stamp and a recording carries. Type-only, 7 lines.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` handling is a small behaviour change for a run that set the variable without a flag: the same effort runs, now passed as the flag and recorded; an invalid value, which the CLI would silently ignore, is now refused at start. A run with `auto` / `unset` is unchanged.
- The gallery refresh (`export/refresh.ts`, `gallery-refresh --model`) takes no effort flag; not in this card. A follow-up can thread the same option if the scheduled task should pin an effort.
- Level names are case-sensitive against the CLI's list (`High` is refused), as the CLI's own help spells them.

## Verification

- Against the real CLI on this box: `effortLevelsFromHelp(claude --help)` = `["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]`; `new ClaudeCodeDriver({ effort: 'xhigh', askEffort: 'low' }).info()` carries `authorEffort: "xhigh", askEffort: "low"`; `{ effort: 'ultra' }` refused with "--effort takes one of the levels `claude` 2.1.325 (Claude Code) accepts (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), not `ultra`". (A throwaway test file, deleted.)
